strings.name: Imran Khan
strings.role: Former Pakistani prime minister · Former cricket captain
strings.summary: Khan moved from cricket into philanthropy and politics, captaining Pakistan’s 1992 World Cup winners, founding PTI in 1996 and serving as premier in 2018–2022. His anti-corruption and welfare-state platform mobilized supporters; his government faced economic and civil-military controversies. Imprisoned since 2023, he has had convictions suspended or overturned while appeals continue. He denies wrongdoing; the government denies that the cases are politically motivated.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: From cricket star to party leader and Pakistani prime minister, his political mobilization and governing proposals have broad social influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: World Cup captain
strings.highlights.h1.text: Captained Pakistan’s winning team at the 1992 Cricket World Cup.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated in philosophy, politics and economics, Keble College, Oxford (1975).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Political mobilization and premiership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded PTI, became prime minister in 2018 and lost office through a 2022 no-confidence vote.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Treatment and prison return
strings.timeline.t1.text: Officials told Reuters he returned to Adiala prison after hospital checks and treatment; lawyers reported declining health.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Land-case sentence
strings.timeline.t2.text: Sentenced to 14 years for land corruption, which he denied; cases later involved suspensions, reversals or appeals.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Imprisonment begins
strings.timeline.t3.text: Imprisoned after a corruption conviction; later changes in that case did not end all detention.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Loses confidence vote
strings.timeline.t4.text: Parliament voted him out after his coalition lost support.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes prime minister
strings.timeline.t5.text: Took office following the election and parliamentary vote.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founds PTI
strings.timeline.t6.text: Entered party politics on anti-corruption and reform proposals.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Cricket World Cup win
strings.timeline.t7.text: Captained the national team, winning alongside his teammates.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Oxford graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from Keble while developing his cricket career.
